description: Classify every vertex of a finite directed game graph as a win, loss, or draw using reverse-edge retrograde propagation.

source.title: Games on arbitrary graphs
source.license_note: The package independently implements the described algorithm. It does not reproduce article prose, source code, or test data.

input.graph_semantics: Repeated directed edges are coalesced; self-loops and directed cycles are allowed.
input.game_semantics: Players alternate moves from the current vertex. A player with no legal outgoing move loses. A position is a draw when neither player can force a win or loss under optimal play.

output.encoding: One byte for vertex_count followed by one status byte per vertex in ascending vertex ID order.

contract.method: Initialize all sinks as losses. Traverse reverse edges: a predecessor of a loss is a win; a predecessor becomes a loss after all distinct successors are known wins. Remaining unresolved vertices are draws.
contract.complexity: O(V+E) time and O(V+E) bounded storage after repeated-edge coalescing.
contract.distinctness: Classifies every position in a cyclic directed graph with retrograde propagation; this is distinct from a subtraction-game Sprague-Grundy mex computation.

workspace.meaning: Sixteen outgoing masks, sixteen incoming-list heads, two 32-entry incoming-edge arrays, sixteen remaining-successor counts, sixteen status entries, sixteen work-queue entries, and seventeen staged output bytes.
